cards.text: Balak, king of Moab, brought in Balaam son of Beor to curse Israel, and twice now it's come out a blessing instead (Numbers 22:4-6; 23:7-24). So Balak takes him to another hilltop, the top of Peor, like a man walking around the house hunting for one more bar of signal (Numbers 23:28). Up there, Balaam sees that it pleases the LORD to bless Israel.

cards.question: This time, Balaam goes off to seek omens like he did before.

cards.text: Instead, Balaam turns his face toward the wilderness. He looks up, sees Israel camped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God comes upon him.

Balaam lifts up an oracle and calls himself a man whose eyes are open, who hears the words of God and sees a vision from the Almighty. Me, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer with my eyes wide open, and all I ever saw was dust.

Then he looks out over the camp and says, “How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!” Balak promised to honor this man richly if he'd curse these people (Numbers 22:17), and he's out here complimenting the tents.

cards.question: Balaam keeps describing Israel's camp spread out below him. What kind of picture does he paint?

answers.text: Gardens and trees growing by water
Walls and towers built for battle
Flocks and herds resting in green fields

cards.text: Balaam says water will flow from Israel's buckets. Then he talks about Israel's king and brings up Agag, a name the Bible later gives a king of the Amalekites (1 Samuel 15:8).

cards.question: Balaam says Israel's king will be greater than Agag.

cards.text: Balaam says God brought Israel out of Egypt with strength like a wild ox. Then he pictures Israel lying down like a lion and asks, “who dares to rouse him?”

cards.question: Balaam ends this oracle with a line about anyone who curses Israel. What does he say happens to them?

answers.text: They are spared in the end

cards.text: Balak's anger burns against Balaam, and he strikes his hands together. And friend, that clap is NOT applause.

cards.question: Balak tells Balaam he has blessed his enemies ___ times now.
Balak has had enough of Balaam's blessings. What does he tell Balaam to do?

answers.text: Flee at once to his home
Try again from a fourth hilltop

cards.question: Balak says it's the LORD who has kept Balaam from his reward.

cards.text: Balaam answers Balak by pointing back to what he already told the messengers Balak sent him. Friend, this is a “per my last email” moment.

cards.question: Balaam says even Balak's house full of silver and gold couldn't get him to do one thing. What is it?

answers.text: Go beyond the command of the LORD
Leave his own people behind for good
Bless the people of Moab instead

cards.question: Balaam says he's going back to his people. But before he leaves, what does he offer Balak?

answers.text: A warning about what Israel will do to his people
A promise to come back and try once more
A blessing on his people for the days ahead

cards.text: So Balaam lifts up another oracle with the same kind of introduction, plus one new line: he has knowledge from the Most High. Hey, I KNOW that name: the One who sent an angel to call me out of that junk drawer.
Then Balaam says something that makes me lean in: “I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near.”

cards.question: Balaam says he sees him, but not now. What does that tell you about the one he's seeing?

answers.text: He's in Israel's camp right now

cards.text: Balaam goes on, “A star will come forth from Jacob, and a scepter will arise from Israel.” A STAR! Berry, one of my cookie cutter kids, the little star, spent every night at the kitchen window asking what was coming next.
Balaam says this coming one will crush the skulls of Moab and strike down all the sons of Sheth. And Balak, king of Moab, is standing right there to hear it.

cards.question: Next Balaam talks about Edom, the nation that came from Esau (Genesis 36:9). He says Edom will become a possession.
Balaam goes on about who will come from Jacob. What does he call him?

cards.text: This ruler will destroy the survivors of the city, Balaam says. Then he sees Amalek, the nation that attacked Israel at Rephidim (Exodus 17:8).

cards.question: Balaam says Amalek was first among the nations. What does he say Amalek's end will be?

cards.text: Next he sees the Kenites, the people of Moses' father-in-law (Judges 1:16), and tells them, “Your dwelling place is secure, and your nest is set in a cliff.” A nest in a CLIFF? That's a home with the security system built right in.

cards.question: Balaam says the Kenites' cliff home will keep them safe forever.
Who does Balaam say will take the Kenites captive?

cards.text: Once more Balaam lifts up an oracle: “Ah, who can live unless God has ordained it?”

cards.question: Balaam says ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus and subdue Asshur and Eber, but they too will ___ forever.
After all the oracles, Balaam goes back to his homeland and Balak goes on his way.
